facts.raw_span: pruritic, pink scaling plaques on her face and neck
lesions subsequently involved her chest, abdomen, and back and flared with sun exposure
Well-demarcated plaques with an overlying scale crust occurring in a photodistributed pattern on the central face, with involvement of chest, abdomen, and back
Antinuclear antibody titers positive at 1:640
Lymphopenia present
Normocytic anemia present
Epidermal acanthosis, spongiosis, and acantholytic keratinocytes
Dense lymphoplasmacellular infiltrate in the dermis, with scattered neutrophils and eosinophils
Granular and linear deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone and abundant intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 in the upper two-thirds of the epidermis
Negative or within normal limits: antiribonucleoprotein, antihistone, antiphospholipid, anti-Smith, anti-Ro/Sjögren syndrome antigen A, and anti-La/Sjögren syndrome antigen B antibodies
Normal C3, C4, CH50, rapid plasma reagin, and creatinine levels
Normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate

concepts.why: The patient's positive antinuclear antibody titers, lymphopenia, and specific histopathological findings are consistent with lupus erythematosus.
The patient's well-demarcated plaques with an overlying scale crust and specific histopathological findings are consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.
The patient's photodistributed lesions and specific histopathological findings are consistent with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
The patient's photodistributed lesions are consistent with polymorphic light eruption.
The patient's specific histopathological findings, including acantholytic keratinocytes and intercellular deposition of IgG, are consistent with pemphigus.

concepts.preferred_label: Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus with Sjögren's Syndrome
concepts.why: The patient's positive antinuclear antibody titers, lymphopenia, and negative antibodies against Sjögren's syndrome antigens are consistent with cutaneous lupus erythematosus with Sjögren's syndrome.

rationales.F01: Pruritic, pink scaling plaques are common in cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F03: Well-demarcated plaques with an overlying scale crust in a photodistributed pattern are characteristic of subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F04: High antinuclear antibody titers are often seen in lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F07: Epidermal acanthosis, spongiosis, and acantholytic keratinocytes are seen in pemphigus and cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F09: Granular and linear deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone is characteristic of lupus erythematosus.
